questions.q:
Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 

NAVIGATE, PCVIGATE, NAXKGATE, ?, NAVIGAVG
questions.s:
Method: Dekh bhai, base word 'NAVIGATE' hai aur step-by-step sirf do hi letters +2 se badh rahe hain, baki word constant reh raha hai.
Step 1: NAVIGATE -> PCVIGATE (N+2=P, A+2=C, baki same).
Step 2: NAXKGATE -> Base word 'NAVIGATE' ke 3rd aur 4th letter ko shift kiya (V+2=X, I+2=K, baki same).
Step 3: Ab Base word 'NAVIGATE' ke 5th aur 6th letter ki baari. (G+2=I, A+2=C). Baki pura word NAVIGATE ki tarah.
Toh word banega: N A V I + I + C + T + E = NAVIICTE.

questions.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. B _ DC _ _ ADD _ BA
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Ye cyclic shift ka classic CGL trap hai. Pura block move ho raha hai.

Ninja Technique:
Pattern check: B A D C
Ab is block ka last letter aage aayega baki shift honge: C B A D
Agla: D C B A
Plugging values: B [A] D C | [C] [B] A D | D [C] B A
Blanks mein aaya: A C B C. Option 2 correct.

questions.q:
Complete the following series from the given options. 

a b _ b a a b x b _ a _ x b a _ b x b a
questions.s:
Method: Total 20 spaces. 4 groups of 5 banate hain:
a b _ b a / a b x b _ / a _ x b a / _ b x b a
Compare karne par pattern 'abxba' banta hai.
Blank spaces in order: x, a, b, a.

questions.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 7, 14, 33, 70, 131, ?
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Wapas cubes ka darshan ho raha hai bhai. 14, 33, 70 sab cubes ke close hain.

Ninja Technique:
$1^3 + 6 = 7$
$2^3 + 6 = 14$
$3^3 + 6 = 33$
$4^3 + 6 = 70$
$5^3 + 6 = 131$
Next hoga $6^3 + 6 = 216 + 6 = 222$.
Option D right answer hai.

questions.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following number series? 5, 7, 9, 11, 18, ?, 34, 35, 59, 67
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Lamba sequence = Alternate series chup ke baithi hai bhai.

Ninja Technique:
Series 1: 5, 9, 18, 34, 59
Diffs: 4, 9, 16, 25 (Perfect squares: $2^2, 3^2, 4^2, 5^2$)
Series 2: 7, 11, ?, 35, 67
Diffs: 4, 8, 16, 32 (Powers of 2: $2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^5$)
Toh $11 + 8 = 19$. Missing term 19 hoga.

questions.q: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 58, 73, 99, 138, 193, ?, 368
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Double nahi triple difference tak jana padega yahan, question thoda calculating hai.

Ninja Technique:
Diff 1: 15, 26, 39, 55, ...
Diff 2: 11, 13, 16, ...
Diff 3: 2, 3, 4, 5
Toh Diff 2 ka next term: $16 + 4 = 20$.
Diff 1 ka next term: $55 + 20 = 75$.
Final Answer: $193 + 75 = 268$.

Pen-Free Observation: Numbers achanak se 18 se 108 ban gaye, matlab multiplication chal raha hai.

Method:
Pichle do numbers ko multiply karke agla number ban raha hai (Fibonacci type multiplication).
3 $\times$ 6 = 18
6 $\times$ 18 = 108
Toh agla hoga 18 $\times$ 108 = 1944.
(Smart calculation: Unit digit dekh, $8 \times 8 = 64$, last mein 4 aayega. Option b is correct).

questions.q:
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 

78, 86, 258, 322, ?
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: 86 se achanak 258 gaya, saaf dikh raha hai ki multiply by 3 hai. Series mein Alternate Plus aur Multiply chal raha hai!

Method:
78 + 8 = 86 (Yahan $+2^3$ hua hai)
86 $\times$ 3 = 258 (Yahan $\times 3^1$ hua hai)
258 + 64 = 322 (Yahan $+4^3$ hua hai)

Pattern set hai: $+2^3, \times 3^1, +4^3$. Agla definitely $\times 5^1$ hoga.
322 $\times$ 5 = 1610.

questions.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 16, 35, ?, 217, 653, 1309
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: 217 se 653 ($\approx \times 3$) and 653 se 1309 ($\approx \times 2$). Alternating multiplication pakdo!

Ninja Technique:
$\rightarrow 16 \times 2 + 3 = 35$
$\rightarrow 35 \times 3 + 2 = 107$
$\rightarrow 107 \times 2 + 3 = 217$
$\rightarrow 217 \times 3 + 2 = 653$
$\rightarrow 653 \times 2 + 3 = 1309$
Toh missing answer 107 hai.

questions.q:
Which of the following alternative will fill the blanks? 

p q _ s t _ q r _ t p _ r s t
questions.s:
Method: Total 15 spaces. 3 groups of 5.
p q _ s t / _ q r _ t / p _ r s t
Saaf dikh raha hai ki 'pqrst' ka hi repetition hai!
Blanks honge: r (pehle group mein), p (dusre group mein), s (dusre mein), q (teesre mein).
Answer: r, p, s, q.

questions.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 6, 16, 29, 62, 121, ?
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Har term double ke aas-paas dikh rahi hai. Multiplying by 2 karke plus/minus check kar.

Ninja Technique:
$\rightarrow 6 \times 2 + 4 = 16$
$\rightarrow 16 \times 2 - 3 = 29$
$\rightarrow 29 \times 2 + 4 = 62$
$\rightarrow 62 \times 2 - 3 = 121$
$\rightarrow 121 \times 2 + 4 = 246$.

questions.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 45, 68, 99, ?, 187, 246, 313
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Differences check kar. Series gap chote hain matlab addition chal raha hai.

Ninja Technique:
Differences: 23, 31, ?, ?, 59, 67
Dhyan se dekh, ye primes hain par alternate skip hoke.
Primes: 23, (skip 29), 31, (skip 37), 41, (skip 43), 47, (skip 53), 59, (skip 61), 67.
Toh agla difference 41 hoga.
$99 + 41 = 140$.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, numbers paas-paas hain, toh sidha difference nikal. Difference 30 ke aas paas ghoom raha hai.

Method (Ninja Technique):
Ulta chalte hain:
258 - 219 = 39
219 - 183 = 36
183 - 150 = 33
Difference mein 3 ka table chal raha hai. Toh agla difference 30 hona chahiye.
150 - 30 = 120.
Option (a) is correct.

Method (Concept Builder): Ye ek standard CGL trap series hai jo frequently repeat hoti hai. Ise hamesha $n^3 + n^2$ format se check karo.

$1^3 + 1^2 = 1 + 1 = 2$
$2^3 + 2^2 = 8 + 4 = 12$
$3^3 + 3^2 = 27 + 9 = 36$
$4^3 + 4^2 = 64 + 16 = 80$
$5^3 + 5^2 = 125 + 25 = 150$

Agla hoga $6^3 + 6^2 = 216 + 36 = 252$.

questions.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 11, 13, 16, 26, 41, 67, 102, ?
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Differences ko dekho, wo perfect squares ke bohot close chal rahe hain.

Ninja Technique:
Differences: 2, 3, 10, 15, 26, 35
Pattern:
$1^2 + 1 = 2$
$2^2 - 1 = 3$
$3^2 + 1 = 10$
$4^2 - 1 = 15$
$5^2 + 1 = 26$
$6^2 - 1 = 35$
Next hoga $7^2 + 1 = 50$.
So, $102 + 50 = 152$.

questions.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 8, 26, 73, 157, 284, 464, 705, 1017, ?
questions.s:
Pen-Free Observation: Double difference nikal ke check kar, series thodi lambi hai toh confirm koi fixed number sequence hoga.

Ninja Technique:
Diffs: 18, 47, 84, 127, 180, 241, 312
Double Diffs: 29, 37, 43, 53, 61, 71
Ye Prime Numbers hain par dhyan se dekh, 1-1 prime number skip kiya hai! (31 skip, 41 skip, 47 skip...)
Toh 71 ke baad 73 skip karke 79 aayega.
Next Diff = $312 + 79 = 391$
Answer = $1017 + 391 = 1408$.
